note: minchah here is the grain offering; "meat" meant food in 1611, but today it suggests flesh.
terumah means something lifted off and set aside, a contribution; "heave" suggests a waving or lifting rite.
megaddef means "reviles/blasphemes"; "reproacheth" is weaker but close.

kjv: fringes in the borders of their (the Israelites') garments
mine: tassels on the corners of their (the Israelites') garments
note: tsitsit means tassels and kanfei means corners (cf. Deut 22:12, "four corners"); "borders" suggests hems.
